summary: This bill increases the rehabilitation tax credit for historic buildings in rural areas, offering a 40% credit for affordable housing projects and a 30% credit for other projects, up to $5,000,000 in expenditures, and allows for the transfer of these credits.

scores.thoughts: This bill increases tax credits, which are a form of government spending through foregone revenue. The expansion of the rehabilitation credit for rural areas, especially for affordable housing, will lead to increased government outlays in the form of tax expenditures.

The bill amends the Internal Revenue Code to enhance rehabilitation tax credits for buildings in rural areas, effectively reducing the tax burden for eligible projects. This represents a targeted tax reduction.

The bill expands and enhances the rehabilitation tax credit for rural historic buildings (raising the rate to 30-40% and allowing credit transfers), which directly reduces federal tax revenue with no offsetting revenue increases or spending cuts. This is the central purpose of the legislation.
